output.interpretation: The request ('lung cancer') doesn't yet define a two-group comparison. The most likely reading is lung tumor tissue (case) vs. normal lung tissue (control) in human bulk RNA-seq. But it could also mean comparing histological subtypes (adenocarcinoma vs. squamous cell carcinoma), a mutation-defined group (e.g., EGFR-mutant vs. wild-type, KRAS, ALK), smokers vs. never-smokers, treatment response or resistance (e.g., parental vs. drug-resistant cell lines, responders vs. non-responders to immunotherapy), or a gene knockdown or overexpression in lung cancer cell lines. Each of these picks out different series and samples, and the tumor vs. normal reading alone would match far more than 10 series.

clarifying_questions.question: Which two groups do you want to compare?
options: Lung tumor vs. adjacent/normal lung tissue
Lung adenocarcinoma vs. lung squamous cell carcinoma
Driver-mutant vs. wild-type tumors (e.g., EGFR, KRAS, ALK, STK11)
Drug-resistant vs. parental/sensitive cells (e.g., osimertinib, cisplatin)
Gene knockdown/knockout/overexpression vs. control in lung cancer cells
clarifying_questions.why: This choice decides which series qualify at all. Tumor vs. normal points to paired surgical cohorts such as GSE81089 and GSE40419. Resistance or perturbation questions point to cell-line experiments, and subtype or mutation questions need tumor cohorts that are annotated for those features.

clarifying_questions.question: Which lung cancer type?
clarifying_questions.why: Histologies can't be swapped for one another. SCLC series are few and rarely include normal controls, while LUAD series are plentiful.

clarifying_questions.question: What kind of sample material?
clarifying_questions.why: You asked not to mix these sample types, so I'll only pick samples from the source you choose.

clarifying_questions.question: For tumor vs. normal, do the samples need to be paired (tumor and normal from the same patient)?
clarifying_questions.why: Requiring paired samples limits the choice to series with matched adjacent normal tissue and changes which GSMs are selected.

clarifying_questions.question: Is there a specific gene or pathway you want to look at?
clarifying_questions.why: A target gene would narrow the choice to perturbation series for that gene, or to cohorts where it varies.
